title: I can greet someone, say who I am, where I'm from and what I do, and ask them the same.
note: Unit 1 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can choose between tú and usted, get a stranger's attention politely, and close a conversation instead of just walking off.
en: I can choose between tú and usted, get a stranger's attention politely, and close a conversation instead of just walking off.

title: I can answer ¿Qué más? or ¿Cómo estás? properly and bounce the question back, with tú or usted.
en: I can answer ¿Qué más? or ¿Cómo estás? properly and bounce the question back, with tú or usted.

title: I can ask simple questions with who, what, where, how many and why, and offer a choice with o.
en: I can ask simple questions with who, what, where, how many and why, and offer a choice with o.

title: I can hold a whole first conversation on my own: greet, swap names and where we're from, thank and say goodbye.
en: I can hold a whole first conversation on my own: greet, swap names and where we're from, thank and say goodbye.

title: I can say I haven't understood, ask what a word means or how it's spelt, and ask someone to repeat.
en: I can say I haven't understood, ask what a word means or how it's spelt, and ask someone to repeat.

title: I can say what I do for a living and ask other people what they do.
en: I can say what I do for a living and ask other people what they do.

title: I can say I'm hungry, thirsty, cold, hot, sleepy or tired.
en: I can say I'm hungry, thirsty, cold, hot, sleepy or tired.

title: I can thank someone for something specific and reply when they thank me.
en: I can thank someone for something specific and reply when they thank me.

title: I can say where I live and work, what I do on a normal day and how I am, and ask simple questions.
note: Unit 2 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can ask which of two things someone prefers and say which I prefer.
en: I can ask which of two things someone prefers and say which I prefer.

title: I can say what I like and dislike and react to someone else's tastes with también, tampoco, sí or no.
en: I can say what I like and dislike and react to someone else's tastes with también, tampoco, sí or no.

title: I can say what I like, want and can do, and what I'm going to do this weekend.
note: Unit 3 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can buy something at a market stall: ask the price, bargain a little, pay and say thanks.
en: I can buy something at a market stall: ask the price, bargain a little, pay and say thanks.

title: I can say what I did last weekend, in order, and say when things happened or will happen.
en: I can say what I did last weekend, in order, and say when things happened or will happen.

title: I can say what I did yesterday and last weekend, in order.
note: Unit 4 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can agree or disagree out loud and correct a wrong fact.
en: I can agree or disagree out loud and correct a wrong fact.

title: I can say who is in my family, how many we are and how old they are.
en: I can say who is in my family, how many we are and how old they are.

title: I can describe a person well enough for someone else to recognise them.
en: I can describe a person well enough for someone else to recognise them.

title: I can introduce someone to somebody else and respond when I'm introduced.
en: I can introduce someone to somebody else and respond when I'm introduced.

title: I can ask and say whose something is.
es: ¿De quién es? —Es de mi hermana. Es mío.

title: I can describe my family and friends: who they are, what they look like, what they're like and how old they are.
note: Unit 5 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say when and where someone was born, how old things are, and how long ago something happened.
en: I can say when and where someone was born, how old things are, and how long ago something happened.

title: I can describe what a place or a person was like and say what happened there and how long ago.
note: Unit 6 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say what there is in my home and neighbourhood and what it's like.
en: I can say what there is in my home and neighbourhood and what it's like.

title: I can ask what something is and point things out: this one, that one, the one over there.
en: I can ask what something is and point things out: this one, that one, the one over there.

title: I can say exactly where something is: next to, opposite, near, between.
en: I can say exactly where something is: next to, opposite, near, between.

title: I can say what there is in my home and neighbourhood, where things are, and how much of everything there is.
note: Unit 7 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say what I know, who and what places I know, and what I have no idea about.
en: I can say what I know, who and what places I know, and what I have no idea about.

title: I can ask and answer about experiences: what I have and haven't done yet, and when it happened.
en: I can ask and answer about experiences: what I have and haven't done yet, and when it happened.

title: I can talk about places I've been and things I've done or haven't done yet, and say what I can and know how to do.
note: Unit 8 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can say sorry for something specific and reply when someone apologises to me.
en: I can say sorry for something specific and reply when someone apologises to me.

title: I can describe my day from waking to bed, saying when things start and finish and how often I do them.
en: I can describe my day from waking to bed, saying when things start and finish and how often I do them.

title: I can scan a sign, timetable, menu or notice for the one fact I need.
en: I can scan a sign, timetable, menu or notice for the one fact I need.

title: I can ask and tell the time and say when things happen in my day.
es: ¿Qué hora es? —Son las tres y media. ¿A qué hora…? —A las ocho de la mañana.

title: I can tell the time and agree a day, time and place to meet, even when the first suggestion doesn't work.
en: I can tell the time and agree a day, time and place to meet, even when the first suggestion doesn't work.

title: I can describe my whole day, say what I'm doing right now and what I have to do.
note: Unit 9 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can order food and drink, ask for what's missing, ask for the bill and pay.
en: I can order food and drink, ask for what's missing, ask for the bill and pay.

title: I can order food and drink, say what I and other people like, and ask for what's missing.
note: Unit 10 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can compare two options on several points and say which I'd pick and why.
en: I can compare two options on several points and say which I'd pick and why.

title: I can describe how my life used to be, and what has changed since.
en: I can describe how my life used to be, and what has changed since.

title: I can describe what my life used to be like and compare it with now.
note: Unit 11 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can react out loud to what someone tells me, sized to the news, and ask a follow-up question.
en: I can react out loud to what someone tells me, sized to the news, and ask a follow-up question.

title: I can talk about the weather today and what it was like.
es: Hoy hace frío. Ayer llovió todo el día.

title: I can tell something that happened to me, with a background scene and a sequence of events.
en: I can tell something that happened to me, with a background scene and a sequence of events.

title: I can tell a short story: what happened, what it was like, and what was going on when it happened.
note: Unit 12 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can ask for and give directions to a real place, step by step.
en: I can ask for and give directions to a real place, step by step.

title: I can ask for the same thing bluntly or very politely, and choose the right level for a friend, a stranger or an official.
en: I can ask for the same thing bluntly or very politely, and choose the right level for a friend, a stranger or an official.

title: I can ask for and give directions, use public transport, and tell a friend or a stranger what to do.
note: Unit 13 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can get around by bus, TransMilenio or taxi: get on, get off, and ask how long it takes.
en: I can get around by bus, TransMilenio or taxi: get on, get off, and ask how long it takes.

title: I can say why I do something and what I do it for.
en: I can say why I do something and what I do it for.

title: I can join short sentences into connected speech, and refer back to things without repeating them.
en: I can join short sentences into connected speech, and refer back to things without repeating them.

title: I can check my own writing for agreement, tense and pronoun mistakes and fix them.
en: I can check my own writing for agreement, tense and pronoun mistakes and fix them.

title: I can write a connected message with reasons and details instead of short separate sentences.
note: Unit 14 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can write the short everyday texts people send: a message, a note, a card, a quick email, with the right opening and closing.
en: I can write the short everyday texts people send: a message, a note, a card, a quick email, with the right opening and closing.

title: I can give a quick verdict on something and agree, half-agree or disagree with someone's opinion.
en: I can give a quick verdict on something and agree, half-agree or disagree with someone's opinion.

title: I can say how I feel physically and what hurts, and ask if someone is OK.
en: I can say how I feel physically and what hurts, and ask if someone is OK.

title: I can say how I and others feel, physically and emotionally, and say what I think of things.
note: Unit 15 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can describe an object: what it looks like, what it's made of and what it's for.
en: I can describe an object: what it looks like, what it's made of and what it's for.

title: I can shop for clothes: ask for a size or colour, try things on, compare, pay, and change something that doesn't fit.
en: I can shop for clothes: ask for a size or colour, try things on, compare, pay, and change something that doesn't fit.

title: I can shop for clothes and other things: ask, compare, try on, pay and return something.
note: Unit 16 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can accept an invitation warmly or with a condition, and turn one down without sounding cold.
en: I can accept an invitation warmly or with a condition, and turn one down without sounding cold.

title: I can suggest a plan, invite someone and ask what they'd like to do.
en: I can suggest a plan, invite someone and ask what they'd like to do.

title: I can say when things start and end and how long they last.
en: I can say when things start and end and how long they last.

title: I can make, accept and turn down plans, and talk about conditions and timing.
note: Unit 17 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can give clear step-by-step instructions.
en: I can give clear step-by-step instructions.

title: I can offer to help someone, or ask if they need help.
en: I can offer to help someone, or ask if they need help.

title: I can travel by bus or plane, book a room, and sort out tickets, luggage and directions.
note: Unit 18 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can give a short talk on a familiar topic: introduce it, make two or three points and close.
en: I can give a short talk on a familiar topic: introduce it, make two or three points and close.

title: I can answer the phone, ask who's calling, put someone on hold and take a message.
en: I can answer the phone, ask who's calling, put someone on hold and take a message.

title: I can talk about my job and studies, read a job ad, and say what a workplace needs.
note: Unit 19 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can give advice, from a gentle suggestion to 'if I were you'.
en: I can give advice, from a gentle suggestion to 'if I were you'.

title: I can say how likely something is, make a guess and make a promise.
en: I can say how likely something is, make a guess and make a promise.

title: I can guess what's going on, make predictions and promises, and give advice with "would" and "should".
note: Unit 20 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can ask a favour, and say yes, a reluctant yes, or no with a reason.
en: I can ask a favour, and say yes, a reluctant yes, or no with a reason.

title: I can ask someone to do something, say what I need from them, and tell them not to do something.
note: Unit 21 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can congratulate someone, wish them well for a trip, a meal or a test, and offer condolences.
en: I can congratulate someone, wish them well for a trip, a meal or a test, and offer condolences.

title: I can congratulate, wish someone well, react to good and bad news, and send a warm message.
note: Unit 22 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can get something sorted on the phone, in a shop or at a desk: explain the problem and what I need.
en: I can get something sorted on the phone, in a shop or at a desk: explain the problem and what I need.

title: I can place events in time: how long ago, how long it's been going on, this week, next month.
en: I can place events in time: how long ago, how long it's been going on, this week, next month.

title: I can deal with a bank, a phone company or a repair: explain the problem, how long it's lasted, and what I need.
note: Unit 23 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can explain a decision, weigh pros and cons, and say what it depends on.
en: I can explain a decision, weigh pros and cons, and say what it depends on.

title: I can explain a decision, weigh reasons for and against, and correct what someone assumed.
note: Unit 24 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can describe a person in depth, compare them with others, tell a moment with them, and pass on what someone told me.
en: I can describe a person in depth, compare them with others, tell a moment with them, and pass on what someone told me.

title: I can walk someone through a place I know, with landmarks, distances and times.
en: I can walk someone through a place I know, with landmarks, distances and times.

title: I can describe a place and a person in detail and pass on what someone told me.
note: Unit 25 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can tell an anecdote in a clear order, keep the listener hooked, and react to theirs.
en: I can tell an anecdote in a clear order, keep the listener hooked, and react to theirs.

title: I can tell an anecdote in a clear order, say how it happened, and react to someone else's.
note: Unit 26 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say what I want others to do and what I hope will happen, with the right strength of hope.
es: Espero que te vaya bien. Ojalá no llueva. Con un poco de suerte, llegamos a tiempo.
en: I hope it goes well for you. I hope it doesn't rain. With a bit of luck we'll make it.

title: I can write a short email, review or message at paragraph length, with a purpose and reactions.
note: Unit 27 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can write a short review and a semi-formal email at paragraph length, keeping usted all the way through.
en: I can write a short review and a semi-formal email at paragraph length, keeping usted all the way through.

title: I can give my opinion, ask for someone else's, and say what I don't think.
es: En mi opinión… / ¿Tú qué piensas? / No creo que sea así.
en: In my opinion… / What do you think? / I don't think it's like that.

title: I can say whether I approve of what someone did, and ask what they made of something.
es: Me parece muy bien que hayas venido. / ¿Qué te pareció?
en: I think it's great you came. / What did you think of it?

title: I can say what I prefer and what I like other people to do, and ask about theirs.
es: Prefiero el bus al TransMilenio. Me encanta que me llamen antes de venir.
en: I prefer the bus to TransMilenio. I love it when people call before coming.

title: I can come down for or against an issue and say why.
es: Estoy en contra de que cierren el parque, porque…
en: I'm against them closing the park, because…

title: I can give and ask for opinions, judge situations, and say what I don't think.
note: Unit 28 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can agree and disagree with a reason attached, from mildly to emphatically.
es: Estoy de acuerdo contigo en que es caro, pero… / ¡Para nada!
en: I agree with you that it's expensive, but… / Not at all!

title: I can say how sure I am, and show that I don't quite believe something.
es: Estoy seguro de que viene. / ¿Tú crees? Lo dudo.
en: I'm sure he's coming. / You think so? I doubt it.

title: I can concede a point and then put the other side, so a disagreement doesn't become a fight.
es: Tienes razón en que es caro, pero también hay que tener en cuenta la calidad.
en: You're right that it's expensive, but you also have to bear quality in mind.

title: I can agree, disagree, doubt and concede without turning it into a fight.
note: Unit 29 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say what annoys me, what I can't stand, when I'm fed up or bored, and when I don't care.
es: Me da rabia que siempre llegue tarde. Estoy harta de esperar. A mí me da igual.
en: It makes me mad that he's always late. I'm fed up with waiting. I don't mind.
note: Emotion hub 3 of 4 (anger, dislike, boredom, indifference). Under-reacting reads as coldness in Spanish.

title: I can say I'm glad, delighted, proud or relieved, and size the reaction to the news.
es: Me alegro muchísimo de que te hayan dado el puesto. ¡Qué alivio!
en: I'm so glad they gave you the job. What a relief!
note: Emotion hub 1 of 4 (pleasure, pride, affection, relief). Intensity is the skill: the biggest form for a small thing reads as sarcasm.

title: I can say what worries, scares, saddens or hurts me, and why.
es: Me preocupa que no conteste. Me duele que no confíes en mí.
en: It worries me that he doesn't answer. It hurts that you don't trust me.
note: Emotion hub 2 of 4 (worry, fear, sadness, emotional hurt).

title: I can react to how someone else feels: show surprise, empathy, calm them down and encourage them.
es: Me imagino. Entiendo que estés molesto. Tranquilo, no es para tanto. ¡Ánimo!
en: I can imagine. I get why you're upset. Easy, it's not that bad. Chin up!
note: Emotion hub 4 of 4 (reacting to others).

title: I can say what something looks, sounds, smells and tastes like, and what bores me or costs me effort.
I can say how other people's actions make me feel, and describe how people change.
note: Unit 30 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can describe a person objectively, then say what I think of them and how they've changed, with an anecdote.
es: Pedro era alto y callado. Con los años ha cambiado mucho: se volvió más abierto.
en: Pedro was tall and quiet. Over the years he's changed a lot: he became more open.

title: I can say how long I've been doing something, and what I still do, have stopped doing or have started again.
I can grab attention before a story and close it so people know it's over.
es: ¿Sabes qué pasó? No te lo vas a creer… Total, que al final todo salió bien.
en: You know what happened? You won't believe it… So anyway, in the end it all worked out.

title: I can tell a story with a real shape — scene, complication, what we did, how it ended — reaching back before its beginning.
es: Aquella tarde todo estaba tranquilo hasta que… Resulta que ya se habían ido.
en: That afternoon everything was calm until… It turns out they'd already left.

title: I can tell a story that reaches back before its own beginning, and report what people said.
note: Unit 31 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can write a personal letter or long message that opens, says why I'm writing, and signs off at the right register.
es: Querida Vale: ¿Cómo estás? Te escribo para contarte… Un abrazo,
en: Dear Vale, how are you? I'm writing to tell you… Hugs,

title: I can say what I and others are good at, find hard, tried to do or managed to do.
I can ask for a favour or help directly, softly, or just by mentioning the problem.
es: Tengo que pedirte un favor… ¿Me harías el favor de recoger a la niña?
en: I need to ask you a favour… Would you do me the favour of picking up my daughter?

title: I can give advice at three levels of directness and match it to how well I know the person.
es: Podrías hablar con él. Yo que tú, lo llamaría. Te recomiendo que vayas al médico.
en: You could talk to him. If I were you, I'd call him. I recommend you see a doctor.

title: I can offer something, invite someone and ask what they feel like doing.
es: ¿Te provoca un tinto? Siéntate, estás en tu casa. Yo invito.
en: Fancy a coffee? Sit down, make yourself at home. It's on me.

title: I can say what I'm planning or thinking of doing, ask about other people's plans, and tell what I meant to do but didn't.
es: Pienso abrir el local en marzo. Pensaba llamarte, pero se me pasó.
en: I'm planning to open the place in March. I meant to call you, but it slipped my mind.

title: I can propose a plan at the right strength, and accept with enthusiasm or with reservations.
es: ¿Qué tal si vamos el sábado? — ¡De una! / Bueno, si insistes…
en: How about we go on Saturday? — Let's do it! / Well, if you insist…

title: I can turn down a request, offer or invitation without causing offence.
es: ¡Qué pena! Me encantaría, pero es que ya tengo planes. Otra vez será.
en: What a shame! I'd love to, but I already have plans. Another time.

title: I can say whether something is on time, late, brought forward or postponed, and how long it takes.
I can give advice at different levels of directness and talk about plans that depend on when things happen.
note: Unit 32 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can describe an object precisely — size, material, state, use — so someone could pick it out, or turn it into a riddle.
es: Es una caja de madera que mide unos treinta centímetros; está llena de cartas viejas.
en: It's a wooden box about thirty centimetres long; it's full of old letters.

title: I can sustain a description of a place for a paragraph and say why it matters to me.
es: Es un apartamento pequeño donde entra mucha luz por dos razones: por una parte… y por otra…
en: It's a small flat that gets a lot of light, for two reasons: on the one hand… and on the other…

title: I can describe a space I'm looking for: its size, what fits, where exactly things are, and what's free, full or left.
I can pick out exactly which one I mean with a relative clause.
es: ¿Cuál? — La que tiene el techo rojo.
en: Which one? — The one with the red roof.

title: I can describe exactly what I'm looking for, even when I don't know if it exists.
note: Unit 33 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can apologise with a reason, and accept someone else's apology gracefully.
es: Perdóname, es que se me olvidó por completo. — Tranquilo, no tiene importancia.
en: Sorry, I completely forgot. — Don't worry, it's nothing.

title: I can explain in detail how a mishap happened: where, how fast, what fell, got dirty, broke or went missing.
I can explain an accident or a mishap, what got lost or broken, and ask for help.
note: Unit 34 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can forbid something clearly, warn someone, and give a direct order when that's what's needed.
es: Está prohibido fumar aquí. ¡Ojo con el escalón! No vayas a tocar eso.
en: Smoking is forbidden here. Watch the step! Don't go touching that.

title: I can ask for permission, give or refuse it, and ask what the rules are.
es: ¿Te importa si abro la ventana? ¿Aquí se puede parquear?
en: Do you mind if I open the window? Can you park here?

title: I can say how I feel physically, in detail, to a doctor or a friend.
es: Me siento fatal desde ayer: me duelen los oídos y tengo escalofríos.
en: I've felt awful since yesterday: my ears hurt and I've got the shivers.

title: I can explain symptoms, understand advice and instructions, and talk about rules.
note: Unit 35 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can give figures, percentages and proportions, and talk about changing prices, deals and things selling out.
I can say what I'm good and bad at, without bragging or underselling.
es: Soy bastante bueno para los números, pero un desastre para los nombres.
en: I'm pretty good with numbers, but hopeless with names.

title: I can talk about money, prices and results, compare figures and draw conclusions.
note: Unit 36 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can ask for information politely with an indirect question.
es: ¿Me podría decir a qué hora abren? Quería saber si todavía hay cupos.
en: Could you tell me what time you open? I wanted to know whether there are still places.

title: I can interrupt politely, check the other person is following, and hold the floor while I think.
es: Perdona que te interrumpa, pero… ¿Me explico?
en: Sorry to interrupt, but… Do you see what I mean?

title: I can show I'm listening, react to a story and keep the other person talking without taking over.
es: ¿En serio? ¿Y entonces qué pasó? No me digas…
en: Seriously? And then what happened? You don't say…

title: I can handle a phone call that has to get something done: ask for someone, take or leave a message, compare options and close properly.
es: ¿Aló? ¿Podría hablar con la doctora Ruiz? — En este momento no se encuentra. ¿Quiere dejarle un mensaje?
en: Hello? Could I speak to Dr Ruiz? — She's not in right now. Would you like to leave a message?

title: I can sort out practical problems in a call: a bad line, a wrong number, a delay, a polite question.
I can soften a request, an opinion or a refusal by shifting the tense.
es: Quería pedirte algo. Yo diría que no es tan grave. Me temo que va a ser difícil.
en: I wanted to ask you something. I'd say it's not that serious. I'm afraid it's going to be hard.

title: I can keep a conversation going: show interest, interrupt, check I understood and pass on messages.
note: Unit 37 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say when I realised or found out something, and how it turned out.
I can bring up news I've heard, say what I know or have no idea about, and react to news.
es: ¿Supiste que cerraron la panadería? — No tenía ni idea. Que yo sepa, seguía abierta.
en: Did you hear they closed the bakery? — I had no idea. As far as I know, it was still open.

title: I can follow a news story, say what happened and why, and react to it.
note: Unit 38 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can explain a topic in writing with definitions, examples, classification and a clear layout.
es: Se trata de… Hay tres tipos: el primero… Por ejemplo… Es como…
en: It's about… There are three kinds: the first… For example… It's like…

title: I can tell from the kind of text what register it needs, and write in it from the first line.
es: Una carta al director: usted, formal, argumentada. Una nota: tú, breve.
en: A letter to the editor: usted, formal, argued. A note: tú, brief.

title: I can give a short prepared talk: hook the audience, map the talk, develop it and close memorably.
es: ¿Sabían que…? Hoy les voy a hablar de… Primero… Para terminar…
en: Did you know that…? Today I'm going to talk to you about… First… To finish…

title: I can make a point land harder: repeat, pile up, single something out.
es: Caminamos horas y horas. Me gusta todo, sobre todo el mar. —¿Vienes? —¡Claro, claro!
en: We walked for hours and hours. I like it all, above all the sea. —Coming? —Of course!

title: I can join ideas with cause, result, concession and contrast, and signpost where my text is going.
es: Como llovía, nos quedamos; sin embargo, al final salimos, así que…
en: Since it was raining we stayed; however, in the end we went out, so…

title: I can write a connected text with an introduction, a development and a conclusion.
note: Unit 39 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can write a 300–400-word composition with a title, an introduction, a development (with the counter-argument) and a conclusion.
es: Título. Introducción: la pregunta. Desarrollo: razones y contraargumento. Conclusión.
en: Title. Introduction: the question. Development: reasons and counter-argument. Conclusion.

title: I can describe temperature, humidity and how a climate feels.
I can talk about how things would be if they were different.
es: Si tuviera más tiempo, aprendería a bucear.
en: If I had more time, I'd learn to dive.
note: The past-unreal half of the old task (si hubiera…, habría…) belongs to u43.

title: I can talk about imaginary situations and say what I would do.
note: Unit 40 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can congratulate, wish people well, propose a toast and reply to good wishes.
es: ¡Felicitaciones! Que cumplas muchos más. Brindo por los novios. — Igualmente.
en: Congratulations! Many happy returns. A toast to the bride and groom. — Same to you.

title: I can reproach someone gently instead of accusing them.
es: Me parece mal que no me avisaras. Podrías haberme llamado.
en: I don't think it was right that you didn't tell me. You could have called me.

title: I can say what I wish were different and report what people asked me to do.
note: Unit 41 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say yes gladly, yes reluctantly, yes-but-only-if, or no with a reason or an alternative.
es: Con mucho gusto. / Bueno, si no hay más remedio… / Sí, pero solo si… / Preferiría que…
en: Gladly. / Well, if there's no other way… / Yes, but only if… / I'd rather…

title: I can ask for help, favours and things — directly or by hinting — and offer my own help politely.
es: ¿Me echas una mano? / Necesito que alguien me revise esto. / Déjeme que la ayude.
en: Can you give me a hand? / I need someone to check this. / Let me help you.

title: I can greet someone warmly after a long time, address people with the right title, and welcome them.
es: ¡Qué milagro! ¡Cuánto tiempo! / Doña Rosa, la buscan. / ¡Qué bueno que hayas venido!
en: Long time no see! / Doña Rosa, someone's asking for you. / So glad you came!

title: I can carry a longer phone call: get put through, ask a chain of questions in usted, and close it.
es: ¿Me comunica con la señora Gómez? … Una cosa más: ¿puedo pagar con tarjeta? … Muy amable, que tenga buen día.
en: Could you put me through to Mrs Gómez? … One more thing: can I pay by card? … Very kind, have a good day.

title: I can thank someone properly, wish them well for the occasion and pass on greetings.
es: No sé cómo agradecértelo. / Le deseo lo mejor. / Dale saludos a tu mamá de mi parte.
en: I don't know how to thank you. / I wish you all the best. / Say hi to your mom for me.

title: I can make the same request or instruction at five levels of formality and pick the one that fits the room.
es: Pásame eso → ¿Me pasas eso? → ¿Me podrías pasar eso? → ¿Sería tan amable de pasármelo? → Le agradecería que me lo hiciera llegar.
en: From 'pass me that' to 'I would be grateful if you could send it to me'.
note: The B2 hinge. Practise one content across friend / colleague / meeting / email to a senior / letter to a newspaper. Check the facts survive and that the formal version is formal, not pompous.

title: I can cushion advice, criticism or bad news so it lands without offence.
es: ¿Puedo decirte una cosa? Yo diría que… Me temo que no va a ser posible.
en: Can I tell you something? I'd say that… I'm afraid that won't be possible.
note: Merges the atenuación lesson's person shifts (tú genérico, uno, nosotros), tense delays (deberías/debías) and pre-announcements.

title: I can make the same request at five levels of formality and know which one fits.
note: Unit 42 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say how something turned out for someone, what they became, and whether it was worth it.
I can express regret, sadness, hurt and disappointment about how things turned out — at the right strength.
es: Es una lástima que no hubiéramos reservado. / Me dolió que no me invitaran. / Me decepcionó su actitud.
en: It's a shame we hadn't booked. / It hurt that they didn't invite me. / Their attitude let me down.

title: I can express relief, hope and resignation.
es: ¡Menos mal que llegaste! / —¿Llegaremos a tiempo? —Eso espero. / Ni modo, otra vez será.
en: Thank goodness you made it! / —Will we make it? —I hope so. / Oh well, next time.

title: I can approve, disapprove and reproach someone for what they did — or didn't do.
es: Me pareció muy bien que se lo dijeras. / No deberías haberle contestado así. / ¿A qué esperas para llamarla?
en: I thought it was right that you told him. / You shouldn't have answered like that. / What are you waiting for?

title: I can talk about wishes and plans — including the ones that never happened.
es: Sueño con tener una finca. / Tenía pensado viajar, pero al final no pude. / ¿Te habría gustado estudiar otra cosa?
en: I dream of having a farm. / I'd planned to travel, but in the end I couldn't. / Would you have liked to study something else?

title: I can talk about what would have happened if things had gone differently, and ask others what they would have done.
es: Si hubiera aceptado ese trabajo, ahora viviría en Cali. ¿Tú qué habrías hecho?
en: If I had taken that job, I'd be living in Cali now. What would you have done?

title: I can talk about what would have happened if things had gone differently, and hedge about what probably did.
note: Unit 43 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can agree and disagree anywhere on the scale, from a casual 'pues sí' to a formal 'no comparto en absoluto'.
es: Pues sí. / En líneas generales estoy de acuerdo, pero… / Comparto su punto de vista. / No estoy en absoluto de acuerdo.
en: Yeah, true. / Broadly I agree, but… / I share your view. / I don't agree at all.

title: I can say how sure I am and how necessary something is, from 'maybe' to 'essential'.
I can give, ask for and grade opinions and evaluations, from assertive to tentative.
es: A mi modo de ver… / Yo diría que… / ¿Qué opinas de que hayan cerrado la biblioteca? / Lo veo difícil.
en: The way I see it… / I'd say… / What do you think of them closing the library? / I don't see it happening.

title: I can propose and suggest things gently, and put conditions on what I agree to.
es: Habría que hablar con ella. / Estaría bien que saliéramos más. / ¿Y si fuéramos a la costa? / Sí, siempre y cuando…
en: Someone ought to talk to her. / It'd be nice to go out more. / What if we went to the coast? / Yes, as long as…

title: I can write a full argumentative text: thesis, cited evidence, the strongest objection answered, and a reservation.
es: Voy a defender que… Un estudio de… muestra que… Se podría objetar que… Sin embargo… Dicho esto, habría que matizar…
en: I will argue that… A study by… shows… One could object that… However… That said, it should be qualified…

title: I can concede a point and then push back, choosing how much ground I give.
es: Puede que tengas razón, pero… / No dudo que sea útil; no obstante…
en: You may be right, but… / I don't doubt it's useful; nevertheless…

title: I can argue a position with evidence, conditions and concessions.
note: Unit 44 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can check a claim, fish for confirmation without asking, confirm firmly, and question something I don't believe.
es: ¿Es verdad eso de que…? / Me contaron que te vas… / Pues claro que sí. / ¡¿De verdad que…?!
en: Is it true that…? / I heard you're leaving… / Of course. / You really…?!

title: I can guess about what has probably happened, with the verb carrying how sure I am.
es: Se habrá quedado dormido. / Lo más probable es que ya se haya ido.
en: He's probably overslept. / Most likely she's already left.

title: I can report events, their causes and approximate figures in a news style.
I can say what I know, how I found out, and what I have no idea about — and ask others the same.
es: Me enteré por un amigo. / ¿Estás al tanto de los cambios? / No tengo ni idea de dónde está.
en: I found out from a friend. / Are you up to date on the changes? / I have no idea where it is.

title: I can follow a news story, summarise it in my own words, and comment on it — including what is only alleged.
es: Según fuentes de la Fiscalía, el concejal habría recibido dinero. Cabe destacar que…
en: According to sources in the Prosecutor's Office, the councillor allegedly received money. It's worth noting…

title: I can follow and write a news report, including what is only alleged.
note: Unit 45 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can say who attended or missed something, when, what people could make out, and what they admitted or denied.
I can say I remember, half-remember, haven't forgotten, or don't recall — and gently dispute someone's version.
es: Me acuerdo perfectamente. / Me suena. / No recuerdo que dijera eso.
en: I remember perfectly. / It rings a bell. / I don't recall her saying that.

title: I can report what people said directly, indirectly and covertly, and choose a reporting verb that shows my stance.
es: Dijo que vendría al día siguiente. / —¿Qué dijo? —Que no. / Reconoció que… / Parece que ya terminaron, según dicen.
en: He said he'd come the next day. / —What did she say? —No. / He admitted… / Apparently they've finished.

title: I can change topic, interrupt politely, hold the floor, and bring a meeting back on track.
es: Por cierto… / Perdone que lo interrumpa, pero… / Déjame terminar. / Como decía…
en: By the way… / Sorry to interrupt, but… / Let me finish. / As I was saying…

title: I can report a whole conversation accurately, and distance myself from what was said.
note: Unit 46 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can turn the volume up or down: intensify, insist, deny flatly, or deny cautiously.
es: Es superbueno. / Te juro que… / ¡Que no, te digo! / No, que yo sepa.
en: It's really good. / I swear… / No, I said! / Not as far as I know.

title: I can move the emphasis in a sentence — clefts, fronting, lo de, focus words — so my point lands where I want it.
es: Lo que pasa es que… / Lo de la financiación es un lío. / Precisamente por eso…
en: The thing is… / The funding business is a mess. / That's exactly why…

title: I can write a story in five stages, with a description and some reported speech folded in.
es: De niña siempre íbamos a la playa… De repente… Llamamos al salvavidas… Al final, todo fue un susto.
en: As a girl we always went to the beach… Suddenly… We called the lifeguard… In the end it was just a scare.

title: I can express joy, excitement, pride, admiration and surprise precisely, not just loudly.
es: Me emociona que vengas. / Estoy orgullosa de ti. / Me extraña que no haya llamado.
en: I'm thrilled you're coming. / I'm proud of you. / It's odd she hasn't called.

title: I can talk about what fascinates, bores or disgusts me and which of two things I'd rather have happen.
es: Me apasiona que toquen en vivo. / ¡Qué pereza! / Prefiero que me digan la verdad a que me mientan.
en: I love it when they play live. / Ugh, can't be bothered. / I'd rather they told me the truth than lied.

title: I can open a story, keep a listener hooked, react as a listener, and wrap it up.
es: ¿Sabes qué? Te cuento… / —¿Que te compraste qué? / Ya me imagino. / Total que…
en: Guess what? Let me tell you… / You bought WHAT? / I can imagine. / So anyway…

title: I can move the emphasis in a sentence so my point lands where I want it.
note: Unit 47 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can describe a person, an object or a place precisely — what it is, its parts, and how it compares.
es: Se trata de una casa de dos pisos que se compone de… A diferencia de la mía, es muy luminosa.
en: It's a two-storey house made up of… Unlike mine, it's very bright.

title: I can present a topic to an audience: open it, develop it by parts, point to the slides, and conclude.
es: Muchos de ustedes seguramente conocerán… Como pueden ver en la pantalla… En definitiva…
en: Many of you will probably know… As you can see on the screen… In short…

title: I can say exactly what a job or process involves, what it depends on and what it needs.
es: Consiste en…, depende de…, cuenta con…

title: I can describe objects, places and processes precisely in writing.
note: Unit 48 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can write a job application, a complaint that gets results, and a formal request.
es: Estimada señora Rodríguez: Me dirijo a usted para… Por todo lo anterior, solicito… Quedo atenta a su respuesta. Cordialmente,
en: Dear Mrs Rodríguez: I am writing to… For all these reasons I request… I look forward to your reply. Regards,

title: I can deal formally with services and contracts: what's available, what's out of order, delivery and pickup.
I can hold a job interview as the candidate: talk about what I'm good at, what I'm not, and why I fit.
es: Tengo facilidad para los números y se me da bien trabajar en equipo; hablar en público me cuesta más.
en: I have a knack for numbers and I'm good at teamwork; public speaking is harder for me.

title: I can write a letter to the editor and a short report weighing the pros and cons of an option.
es: Me dirijo a ustedes en relación con el artículo publicado el… Entre las ventajas destaca…
en: I am writing regarding the article published on… Among the advantages…

title: I can write a formal letter: an application, a complaint and a request.
note: Unit 49 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can advise, warn and — if it comes to it — threaten.
es: Lo mejor sería que fueras al médico. / ¡Ojo con…! / Te advierto que… / Si no lo terminas, …
en: It'd be best if you saw a doctor. / Watch out for…! / I'm warning you… / If you don't finish it, …

title: I can express annoyance, exasperation, nerves and outrage at the right pitch.
es: Me da rabia que… / Me indigna que… / Estoy harta de que… / ¡Ya basta!
en: It annoys me that… / It outrages me that… / I'm fed up with… / Enough!

title: I can console, reassure and encourage someone, and show I'm on their side.
es: Te entiendo perfectamente. / Ya pasó. / No tengas miedo de equivocarte.
en: I completely understand. / It's over now. / Don't be afraid of getting it wrong.

title: I can express worry, fear and embarrassment, from mild to extreme.
es: Me preocupa que… / Me da pánico que… / Me da vergüenza pedirle otra vez.
en: It worries me that… / I'm terrified that… / I'm embarrassed to ask him again.

title: I can set conditions and limits and hold my position, politely, whatever happens.
es: Mientras…, hasta que no…, pase lo que pase…, estoy dispuesto a…, ni aunque…

title: I can handle a conversation where we want different things: soften, concede, hold my ground and agree an outcome.
es: Lamento lo del otro día… No es que no quiera, es que… Puede que tengas razón, pero… ¿Y si lo dejamos así?
en: I'm sorry about the other day… It's not that I don't want to, it's that… You may be right, but… What if we leave it like this?

title: I can handle a conversation where we want different things, and keep it civil.
note: Unit 50 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can recognise everyday Spain-Spanish reactions in what I read and know the Latin American equivalent.
es: vale = listo / qué rollo = qué pereza / echar de menos = extrañar / ¡anda! = ¡uy!
en: Spain's everyday words mapped to ours.
note: Recognition only; the B2 lessons were written in Peninsular Spanish and these are the items converted elsewhere.

title: I can read Spanish from Spain and other countries, and understand vosotros and Spain's use of the past.
note: Unit 51 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can tell a life story with precise time markers and vivid turns: back in the day, it broke out, I ended up…
en: I can tell a life story with precise time markers and vivid turns: back in the day, it broke out, I ended up…

title: I can choose a tense or mood on purpose and explain why I chose it.
note: Annotated-writing task: one line per finite verb saying why this tense/mood and not the nearest one.

title: I can tell an anecdote with a hook, a complication, a twist at the end and the dialogue reported inside it.
note: Five stages: situation, complication, action, resolution, final twist.

title: I can choose any tense or mood deliberately and explain why I chose it.
note: Unit 52 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can say exactly how sure I am of a claim, and report what was hinted, covered up or came to light.
en: I can say exactly how sure I am of a claim, and report what was hinted, covered up or came to light.

title: I can check what I've heard indirectly, confirm it, or let someone know I suspect what they're implying.
I can criticise or correct something firmly without pointing a finger at anyone.
I can say exactly how sure I am — from proven fact to hunch — and what I do and don't know.
I can rephrase, correct myself, sum up, or set an objection aside without answering it.
I can report what someone said and, through the verb I choose, show how it should be taken.
I can pass on claims and rumours without vouching for them myself.
I can report claims, rumours and other people's ideas without vouching for them.
note: Unit 53 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can use colourful exaggeration and ironic idioms — and catch them when others use them on me.
en: I can use colourful exaggeration and ironic idioms — and catch them when others use them on me.

title: I can react to people and news the way Colombians do: exclamations, ironic imperatives and understatement.
es: ¡Mira que…!, ¡la cara que puso!, tiene su truco, ¿cómo así?, ¡dale!

title: I can say something with real force — or with pointed understatement — and judge people in a single image.
I can deny, refuse or contradict without a plain 'no' — from a softened 'no digo que…' to '¡ni loco!'.
I can be ironic in Spanish, and I can tell when someone is being ironic with me.
I can use and catch irony, understatement and implied meaning.
note: Unit 54 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can handle formal terms in writing: deadlines, availability, approval, postponements and how costs are split.
en: I can handle formal terms in writing: deadlines, availability, approval, postponements and how costs are split.

title: I can write a complaint letter that gives the context, states each problem precisely and proposes a concrete solution.
I can write to an institution in a consistent formal register without sounding like a form.
I can write a commercial letter that gets attention, builds interest and desire, then asks for action.
I can read and write institutional and legal Spanish without sounding like a form.
note: Unit 55 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can agree fully or partly, disagree softly or flatly, and concede a point before I counter it.
I can write a sustained argumentative essay: the contested question, my position, the strongest counter-case and an honest reservation.
I can trace causes and roots, generalise carefully and say to what extent something is true in an essay.
en: I can trace causes and roots, generalise carefully and say to what extent something is true in an essay.

title: I can describe how things rise, fall and change — gradually, suddenly or completely.
en: I can describe how things rise, fall and change — gradually, suddenly or completely.

title: I can ask for and give opinions with the right weight for the setting, from an interview to a chat.
I can take part in a formal meeting or public debate on my own field and defend a position.
note: Lectures and sermons are reception only.

title: I can write an academic or expository text with a narrowing introduction, a stated roadmap and a conclusion that names what is still unresolved.
I can write a sustained argumentative essay and defend it.
note: Unit 56 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.

title: I can express resignation, guilt, patience and how I'm coping with something hard.
en: I can express resignation, guilt, patience and how I'm coping with something hard.

title: I can describe thinking a decision through: racking my brain, sleeping on it, the penny dropping.
en: I can describe thinking a decision through: racking my brain, sleeping on it, the penny dropping.

title: I can show empathy, calm someone down and push them to go for it.
I can express a complicated or mixed emotion precisely, including through understatement and the body.
I can say how scared, fed up, angry or relieved I am at native strength.
I can talk about regret, embarrassment, disappointment and resignation.
I can talk about longings, half-formed plans, firm resolutions, preferences and indifference.
I can express complex emotions precisely: regret, resignation, relief, mixed feelings.
note: Unit 57 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can describe how things feel, sit, move and where they are — texture, temperature, position, distance.
en: I can describe how things feel, sit, move and where they are — texture, temperature, position, distance.

title: I can describe the physical and temporal world with native precision.
note: Unit 58 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can advise, warn, threaten, reproach and offer help, and hear which of these someone is doing.
I can recognise Colombian ways of saying common idioms and switch between them and neutral Spanish.
en: I can recognise Colombian ways of saying common idioms and switch between them and neutral Spanish.

title: I can introduce a story, check that my listener is following, change the subject and close a conversation politely.
I can give orders and make requests anywhere on the scale from blunt to ceremonious, and answer them.
I can invite and propose, and accept or refuse with or without conditions.
I can greet, answer 'how are things?', congratulate, thank, apologise, give condolences and say goodbye at the right register.
I can understand regional Colombian voices and adapt my own register to who I'm talking to.
note: Unit 59 goal; tested on the Output day.

title: I can judge something publicly — approve it, find it in poor taste, or condemn it.
I can rate a work or a place on a fine scale in a review — from 'leaves a lot to be desired' to 'one of a kind'.
en: I can rate a work or a place on a fine scale in a review — from 'leaves a lot to be desired' to 'one of a kind'.

title: I can write a critical review in my own voice, with a clear verdict backed by evidence from the work.
I can write and defend a critical review in my own voice.
note: Unit 60 goal; tested on the Output day and the checkpoint.
